## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

MainActivity — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/MainActivity.kt

## Trigger

The launch intent carrying `WatchRaceComplicationDataSourceService.EXTRA_TAPPED_DESTINATION`, delivered to `MainActivity` when the complication is tapped — observed only on the already-alive path, through `onNewIntent`

## Today

`WatchRaceComplicationDataSourceService.onComplicationRequest` builds a `PendingIntent` targeting `MainActivity` with `EXTRA_TAPPED_DESTINATION` set to the current `WatchDestination`'s name. `MainActivity.onNewIntent` reads that extra and calls `navigator.navigateTo(WatchDestination.valueOf(extra))`. `MainActivity.onCreate` never reads `intent`'s extras — it only sets `setContent` from `navigator.current`. The manifest's `<activity android:name=".MainActivity">` declares no `android:launchMode`, so it defaults to `standard`: a tap does not redeliver to an existing instance's `onNewIntent`, it starts a new instance whose entry point is `onCreate`. `onNewIntent` is therefore reachable only in the narrow case where the system happens to redeliver to the same task without creating a fresh instance; in every ordinary case — process alive with the activity backgrounded, or process dead — the tap runs `onCreate`, which ignores `getIntent()`'s extra, and the destination is lost.

## Expected

Tapping the complication navigates to the carried destination on every path: `MainActivity`'s manifest declaration carries `android:launchMode="singleTop"` so a tap while the activity is already the top of its task redelivers through `onNewIntent` instead of spawning a new instance, and `MainActivity.onCreate` reads `EXTRA_TAPPED_DESTINATION` off `intent` (the activity's own launch intent) the same way `onNewIntent` does, calling `navigator.navigateTo(WatchDestination.valueOf(extra))` when it is present, so the destination survives a fresh process start.
